verses.speaker: Dhritarashtra
verses.tr: Dhritarashtra said: Sanjaya, on the holy field of Kurukshetra, gathered and eager to fight, what did my sons and the sons of Pandu do?

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.tr: Sanjaya said: Seeing the Pandava army drawn up for battle, King Duryodhana went to his teacher Drona and said:

verses.speaker: Duryodhana (told by Sanjaya)
verses.tr: Teacher, look at this mighty army of the sons of Pandu, arranged by the son of Drupada, your own clever student.

verses.speaker: Duryodhana (told by Sanjaya)
verses.tr: Here are heroes and great archers, equal in battle to Bhima and Arjuna: Yuyudhana, Virata and the great chariot-warrior Drupada;

verses.speaker: Duryodhana (told by Sanjaya)
verses.tr: Dhrishtaketu, Chekitana and the brave king of Kashi; Purujit, Kuntibhoja and Shaibya, the best of men;

verses.speaker: Duryodhana (told by Sanjaya)
verses.tr: mighty Yudhamanyu and brave Uttamaujas, the son of Subhadra, and the sons of Draupadi, all of them great chariot-warriors.

verses.speaker: Duryodhana (told by Sanjaya)
skt: अस्माकं तु विशिष्टा ये तान्निबोध द्विजोत्तम
नायका मम सैन्यस्य संज्ञार्थं तान्ब्रवीमि ते
verses.tr: And now, best of brahmins, know the leaders of our own army. I name them for you.

verses.speaker: Duryodhana (told by Sanjaya)
verses.tr: Yourself, Bhishma, Karna and Kripa, ever victorious in battle; Ashvatthama, Vikarna and the son of Somadatta.

verses.speaker: Duryodhana (told by Sanjaya)
skt: अन्ये च बहवः शूरा मदर्थे त्यक्तजीविताः
verses.tr: And many other heroes, ready to give their lives for me, armed with many weapons and all skilled in war.

verses.speaker: Duryodhana (told by Sanjaya)
verses.tr: Our army, guarded by Bhishma, seems beyond measure, while theirs, guarded by Bhima, is limited. (Some commentators read it the other way round: ours is not enough, theirs is enough.)

verses.speaker: Duryodhana (told by Sanjaya)
verses.tr: So all of you, standing firm at your posts in every formation, must protect Bhishma above all.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.tr: To cheer Duryodhana, the mighty grandsire Bhishma, eldest of the Kurus, roared like a lion and blew his conch loudly.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.tr: Then conches, kettledrums, tabors, drums and horns all sounded at once, and the noise was tremendous.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.tr: Then Krishna and Arjuna, seated in their great chariot yoked to white horses, blew their divine conches.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.tr: Krishna blew Panchajanya, Arjuna blew Devadatta, and Bhima of fearsome deeds blew his great conch Paundra.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.tr: King Yudhishthira, son of Kunti, blew Anantavijaya; Nakula and Sahadeva blew Sughosha and Manipushpaka.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.tr: The king of Kashi, a fine archer, the great chariot-warrior Shikhandi, Dhrishtadyumna, Virata and the unconquered Satyaki,

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.tr: Drupada, the sons of Draupadi, and the strong-armed son of Subhadra, all blew their own conches, O king.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.tr: That tremendous sound, echoing through sky and earth, shook the hearts of Dhritarashtra's sons.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.tr: Then, as the weapons were about to clash, Arjuna, whose flag bore Hanuman, looked at Dhritarashtra's sons standing ready and raised his bow,

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.tr: and said to Krishna: "Achyuta, place my chariot between the two armies,

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.tr: so that I may see those standing here eager to fight, with whom I must fight in this battle.

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.tr: I want to see who has gathered here ready to fight, wanting to please the wicked-minded son of Dhritarashtra."

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.tr: Sanjaya said: Asked this by Arjuna, Krishna drove the finest of chariots and stopped it between the two armies,

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.tr: in front of Bhishma, Drona and all the kings, and said: "Arjuna, look at these Kurus gathered here."

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.tr: There Arjuna saw, standing in both armies, fathers and grandfathers, teachers, uncles, brothers, sons, grandsons and friends,

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.tr: fathers-in-law and well-wishers. Seeing all these relatives standing there,

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.tr: Arjuna was filled with deep pity and said sadly: "Krishna, seeing my own people standing here eager to fight,

verses.speaker: Arjuna
skt: सीदन्ति मम गात्राणि मुखं च परिशुष्यति
verses.tr: my limbs give way, my mouth is dry, my body trembles and my hair stands on end.

verses.speaker: Arjuna
skt: न च शक्नोम्यवस्थातुं भ्रमतीव च मे मनः
verses.tr: My bow Gandiva slips from my hand, my skin burns, I cannot stand steady, and my mind is spinning.

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.tr: I see bad omens, Keshava, and I see no good in killing my own people in battle.

verses.speaker: Arjuna
skt: न काङ्क्षे विजयं कृष्ण न च राज्यं सुखानि च
किं नो राज्येन गोविन्द किं भोगैर्जीवितेन वा
verses.tr: Krishna, I do not want victory, or a kingdom, or pleasures. What use is a kingdom to us, Govinda, or enjoyment, or even life,

verses.speaker: Arjuna
skt: येषामर्थे काङ्क्षितं नो राज्यं भोगाः सुखानि च
त इमेऽवस्थिता युद्धे प्राणांस्त्यक्त्वा धनानि च
verses.tr: when the very people for whom we want a kingdom and pleasures stand here in battle, ready to give up their lives and wealth?

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.tr: Teachers, fathers, sons, grandfathers, uncles, fathers-in-law, grandsons, brothers-in-law and other relatives.

verses.speaker: Arjuna
skt: अपि त्रैलोक्यराज्यस्य हेतोः किं नु महीकृते
verses.tr: I do not want to kill them, Madhusudana, even if they kill me, not even to rule the three worlds, let alone this earth.

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.tr: What happiness could we have from killing the sons of Dhritarashtra, Janardana? Only sin would come to us from killing these attackers.

verses.speaker: Arjuna
skt: स्वजनं हि कथं हत्वा सुखिनः स्याम माधव
verses.tr: So we should not kill the sons of Dhritarashtra, our own family. How could we be happy after killing our own people, Madhava?

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.tr: Even if they, blinded by greed, see nothing wrong in destroying a family and no sin in betraying friends,

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.tr: why should we, who can see the wrong in destroying a family, not turn away from this sin, Janardana?

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.tr: When a family is destroyed, its age-old traditions are lost; and when dharma is lost, wrongdoing takes over the whole family.

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.tr: When wrongdoing spreads, Krishna, the women of the family go astray, and from that comes confusion of the social order.

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.tr: This confusion drags the family and its destroyers to hell, and their ancestors fall, deprived of the offerings of food and water.

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.tr: Through these wrongs of the family-destroyers, the lasting duties of community and family are ruined.

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.tr: We have heard, Janardana, that people whose family duties are destroyed live in hell for a long time.

verses.speaker: Arjuna
skt: अहो बत महत्पापं कर्तुं व्यवसिता वयम्
verses.tr: Alas! What a great sin we are set on doing, ready to kill our own people out of greed for the pleasures of a kingdom!

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.tr: It would be better for me if the sons of Dhritarashtra, weapons in hand, killed me in battle while I stood unarmed and did not fight back."

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.tr: Sanjaya said: Having said this on the battlefield, Arjuna threw down his bow and arrows and sank down on the seat of the chariot, his mind overwhelmed with grief.
